newsitem.title: USA: Czech "Kolya" wins Oscar for best foreign film.
newsitem.headline: Czech "Kolya" wins Oscar for best foreign film.

text.p: The politically-charged "Kolya" brought home an Academy Award on Monday for the writer/director team of Jan Sverak and his father, Zdenek, from the Czech Republic.

"Kolya" tells of the re-awakening of an ageing cellist as he and a Russian boy journey through the Czech countryside on the eve of Prague's "Velvet Revolution" in 1989. It had been the pre-Oscar favourite after winning the Golden Globe award that is given by the foreign press in Los Angeles.

When he accepted his award at the Shrine Auditorium in front of many of Hollywood's elite moviemakers, the younger Sverak looked at Oscar, smiled and said, "You are going to Prague." He then thanked "everyone at home."

In "Kolya," the elder cellist leaves the Philharmonic orchestra for political reasons and takes to the country. He spends his days playing funerals and chasing women until in a scheme that goes wrong, he ends up with custody of the Russian youngster, Kolya.
"The film is about how the understanding between nations is much more important than the power," Sverak told reporters backstage at the Oscars.
He also said the movie, which deals with Russian influence over the former Czechoslovakia, is about "forgive and forget."

The blend of Czech comedy and political drama has struck at the hearts of the people of the Czech Republic. It recently surpassed the 1 million attendance mark, making it the most successful Czech film of the past five years.
The Sverak writing and directing team had been nominated once before, in 1992 for "Elementary School," but did not win that year.
